clue.text: Give a large amount in harmless display of aggression?

parts.note: to hand something over is to give it
informal: bags of something is plenty of it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a big donation counts as a gentle show of hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handbags' (as in 'handbags at dawn') is British slang for a scuffle, especially between footballers, that is all posturing and no real harm.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a confrontation with much pushing and shouting but no real violence, likened to women swinging purses.

clue.text: Start unconventionally, manouevring two into employ

indicators.note: one part is put into the middle of another word
manoeuvring something moves it about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word two, rearranged
to hire someone is to employ them

explanation.surface: Advice on taking on staff by shuffling a pair of people into jobs in an unusual way.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters sit between the H and the IRE of the employing word: H-OTW-IRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To hot-wire a car is to start its engine without a key by connecting the ignition wires directly.

clue.text: French city has eminently risen — to an extent

indicators.note: in a down clue, something that has risen reads from bottom to top
only partly, so just a stretch of the letters in these words is wanted

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A French town has gone up in the world, somewhat.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters S-E-M-I-N sit across 'has eminently'; read upwards they give NIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Nîmes is a city in southern France, famous for its Roman arena and as the origin of denim.

clue.text: Arm, or back, or otherwise, a type of lawyer

definitions.note: the answer is the qualifier in the phrase barrack-room lawyer

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: the letters of these words taken together

explanation.surface: A lawyer weighing up whether to arm, support, or do something else.
explanation.walkthrough: A barrack-room lawyer is a soldier, or anyone, who argues about rules and rights without real knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase barrack-room lawyer names a self-appointed, argumentative expert on regulations, originally among soldiers in quarters.

clue.text: After golf day, sank unusual port

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
D is the abbreviation for day
the word sank, rearranged

explanation.surface: After a day on the golf course, someone sank a remarkable putt in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the rearranged letters come after the golf and day letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gdańsk is a major Polish seaport on the Baltic coast, birthplace of the Solidarity movement.

clue.text: Deal won't, oddly, start

indicators.note: oddly points to the letters in odd-numbered positions only

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A negotiator complains that the agreement strangely refuses to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn means the beginning of something, as in the dawn of a new era, a figurative start.

clue.text: Embassy staffer not drinking: a pain all round!

indicators.note: all round means surrounding, so these pieces go either side of another

parts.note: taken as written
TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A sober diplomat is found to be a bore by everyone around.
explanation.walkthrough: TT stands for teetotal, a person who never drinks alcohol. 'Pain' reads as an insult to the diplomat, but it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a person on an ambassador's staff with a particular specialism, such as a military or cultural attaché.

clue.text: Marines arriving in numbers bringing standards

indicators.note: arriving in a place means going inside it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: NOS is short for numbers
RM stands for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Troops landing in large numbers set the benchmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Norms are accepted standards of behaviour or performance, the usual expected levels.

clue.text: Watch, perhaps, maiden involved in row

indicators.note: something involved in another is caught up inside it

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Look out, maybe a young woman is caught up in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests an argument, but here it is a line of seats. A maiden over in cricket is one with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is one example of a device for measuring time, hence the 'perhaps' marking an example.

clue.text: Increasingly perceptive, of abnormal stature

indicators.note: abnormal means not in its usual form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of this word

explanation.surface: Someone of unusual height grows ever more insightful.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means shrewd and perceptive; the comparative form means more so, matching 'increasingly'.

clue.text: Sort of race featuring a tie between each team?

definitions.text: Sort of race featuring a tie between each team?

parts.words: Sort of race featuring a tie between each team?
parts.note: surface reading: a contest where every side ends up drawn, scores level; setter's reading: each pair of runners has their adjacent legs tied together

explanation.surface: A race in which every team finishes level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie' looks like a draw; in fact it is a strap binding two runners' legs, leaving three legs per pair.
explanation.definitionFit: In this sports-day race, two partners run with an inner leg strapped together, so the pair has three legs between them.

clue.text: Picks out one police officer

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
DS is a detective sergeant

explanation.surface: One officer singles out a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: To ID someone is to identify them, as in picking a suspect out of a line-up.

clue.text: Removes a bishop's pamphlets

parts.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, plus the S of the possessive
tracts are short pamphlets, often religious

explanation.surface: Someone takes away a churchman's leaflets.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract something is to take it away or extract it, a formal verb for removing.

clue.text: I've found it some mistake, ruefully reflecting

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run the other way
some of the words, meaning only part of their letters is used

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: Someone spots an error and thinks about it with regret.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters A-K-E-R-U-E sit across 'mistake, ruefully'; read right to left they spell EUREKA.
explanation.definitionFit: Eureka is Greek for 'I have found it', the exclamation attributed to Archimedes on his discovery.

clue.text: Change of plan on Thursday, something writer needs

parts.note: re means on, concerning
TH is short for Thursday
a pen writer needs ink

explanation.surface: A writer's plans change on Thursday for some reason.
explanation.definitionFit: A rethink is a reconsideration of a plan that typically leads to altering it.

clue.text: We settled into cosy place, most modern!

indicators.note: to settle into a place is to sit inside it

parts.note: a nest is a snug, cosy place
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple announce they have moved into the most up-to-date snug home.
explanation.definitionFit: Newest is the superlative of new, so the most recent or modern of all.

clue.text: Without pyjama jacket perhaps, so slept unsoundly

indicators.note: unsoundly means in a disturbed, faulty way, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone without a pyjama top had a restless night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsoundly' fits the surface of poor sleep, but it signals the letter shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Topless means with the upper body bare, and missing a pyjama jacket is one example of that state.

clue.text: Gesture aligns, somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the letters of this word

explanation.surface: A movement somehow lines things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal is a gesture or action made to convey a message, such as a wave or nod.

clue.text: Allow writer one's eraser at the start

parts.note: an author is a writer
I is one, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: just its first letter

explanation.surface: Permit the writer to use their rubber at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: To authorise is to give official permission for something, to allow it formally.

clue.text: Missile, limited in range, heading off

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, and it is taken off

parts.note: narrow means restricted in scope or range

explanation.surface: A short-range rocket is setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' reads like a missile departing, but it tells you to drop the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a missile shot from a bow, a projectile in the original sense of the word.

clue.text: Jump is hard work!

parts.note: H is hard, as in pencil grades
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone complains that leaping is strenuous.
explanation.definitionFit: To hop is to make a small jump, especially on one foot.

clue.text: Scavenger's intense desire to enter hotel area

indicators.note: something that enters goes inside, so one piece sits within the others

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
A is the abbreviation for area
a yen is a strong longing

explanation.surface: A scavenging animal longs to get into the hotel grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The longing goes between the hotel and area letters: H-YEN-A.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyenas are African carnivores well known for feeding on carcasses left by other predators.

clue.text: Damage an arm in making film

indicators.note: damaging something knocks it out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: An actor injures a limb while shooting a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain Man is the 1988 film starring Dustin Hoffman and Tom Cruise that won the Best Picture Oscar.

clue.text: Brent's fliers?

parts.note: surface reading: aircraft or leaflets belonging to someone called Brent; setter's reading: the brent is a kind of small dark bird, and these are its kind

explanation.walkthrough: Brent looks like a person's name (David Brent of TV's The Office), but the brent is a species of small dark goose.
explanation.definitionFit: Brent geese are small, dark waterfowl that migrate to Britain's coasts in winter, so they are Brent's fliers.

clue.text: Came to window to look there, finally

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the words

parts.note: the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: Someone regained consciousness and went to the window to peer out at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came to' looks like the start of a journey to the window; it is the definition, meaning regained consciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is to regain consciousness, and woke likewise means became conscious again.

clue.text: Happy kid's best clothes

parts.note: glad means happy
to kid someone is to rag, or tease, them
the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A cheerful child's Sunday outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is the verb meaning to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is an informal idiom for one's smartest clothes, worn for a special occasion.
